newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa, Stet lead Spain's Retevision race.
newsitem.headline: Endesa, Stet lead Spain's Retevision race.

text.p: Recent adjustments in the three groups of bidders for the forthcoming privatisation of Retevision have strengthened the position of the Endesa-Stet team, analysts said on Wednesday.

"It is difficult to say, but the BCH team was weakened by the decision of Deutsche Telekom to give up, and now this group has the same possibilities as the one led by Endesa and Stet," a Spanish analyst said.
On Monday the three competitors for the 60 percent privatisation of what will be Spain's second basic telephone operator presented the final composition of each group.

Once-favourite Opera, which teams up BCH, France Telecom and Sprint, announced the withdrawal of Deutsche Telekom. Meanwhile its main rival, led by Endesa and Stet, won additional backing from several saving banks.

Unisource has been eliminated because it bid too late, while a third group, which comprises only Mannesmann, seems weak as it has no domestic backing, and only the tacit backing of AT&T, analysts said.
The Endesa and Stet group have the strong card of good infrastructure, after announcing deals with regional electric utilities that will contribute their fibre optic network.
In this group are also Union Fenosa, BBK, Kutxa, Unicaja, Caja de Ahorros del Mediterraneo, Ibercaja, Caja Navarra and the Basque regional telecom operator Euskatel.
One analyst said Euskatel would complement Stet's technical contribution, while saving banks with good regional distribution will give their support in developing business.

Opera, in an attempt to catch up on infrastructure, made a deal with Spanish railways Renfe to use its fibre-optics network. And some analysts still say it has very good chances of winning the auction.
"We don't doubt Stet's technological ability, but rather its international expansion policy," another analyst said.
A third analyst at a foreign bank said: "France Telecom is still the best bid. But Stet may be willing to pay a higher price. In the end it will depend on how greedy the government is".
In the meantime Telefonica de Espana seems to be making the most of the competition between the different groups.
"Our sector analyst increased his share price target for Telefonica, partly because of the withdrawal of Deutsche Telekom and the less certain role of AT&T," an analyst said.
The three groups have until June 9 to present their offers, with a minimum established price tag of 45.6 billion pesetas ($316.8 million) already set by the government for Retevision.
Following this, the winning group will be committed to fully underwrite a 10 percent capital increase, with an outlay of at least 25.33 billion pesetas more.
